script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 14, 2026.

The study enrolled and randomized 283 very preterm infants (mean [SD] gestational age, 30.2 [2.2] weeks; 161 girls [57%]); 143 received procalcitonin- and presepsin-guided treatment and 140 received universal antibiotic treatment.

articles.title: Procalcitonin- and Presepsin-Guided Antibiotics for Early-Onset Sepsis in Preterm Infants: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: This randomized multicenter noninferiority clinical trial was conducted in 17 Italian neonatal intensive care units between June 1, 2023, and January 31, 2025, among preterm infants born at 25 weeks and 0 days to 31 weeks and 6 days of gestation. Enrolled infants were randomly allocated to receive either PCT- and P-SEP-guided antibiotic treatment, administered if PCT and P-SEP levels exceeded prespecified thresholds, or universal antibiotic treatment for EOS. The composite primary outcome was defined as survival without late-onset sepsis (LOS), bronchopulmonary dysplasia, grade 3 or 4 intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), grade 2 or higher necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), periventricular leukomalacia (PVL), or stage 3 or higher retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). The study enrolled and randomized 283 very preterm infants (mean [SD] gestational age, 30.2 [2.2] weeks; 161 girls [57%]); 143 received procalcitonin- and presepsin-guided treatment and 140 received universal antibiotic treatment. The primary outcome did not differ between the PCT- and P-SEP-guided treatment group and the universal antibiotic treatment groups (76 of 143 [53%] vs 77 of 140 [55%]; risk difference, -1.8 percentage points; 90% CI, -11.9 to 8.3 percentage points; P = .32).
